Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github. **Learn more in the [official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview)**. ## Get started > [!NOTE] > Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below. For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the [setup documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup). 1. Install Claude Code: **MacOS/Linux (Recommended):** ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` **Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):** ```bash brew install --cask claude-code ``` **Windows (Recommended):** ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` **WinGet (Windows):** ```powershell winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode ``` **NPM (Deprecated):** ```bash npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ``` 2. Navigate to your project directory and run `claude`. ## Plugins Anthropic's Claude Code plugins are developed in [claude-plugins-official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official). See the [plugins directory](./plugins/README.md) for more about plugins. ## Reporting Bugs We welcome your feedback. Use the `/bug` command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues). ## Connect on Discord Join the [Claude Developers Discord](https://anthropic.com/discord) to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community. ## Data collection, usage, and retention When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the `/bug` command. ### How we use your data See our [data usage policies](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). ### Privacy safeguards We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training. For full details, please review our [Commercial Terms of Service](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms) and [Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy).
readmeHtml:
Claude Code

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands. Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.

Learn more in the official documentation.

Get started

Note

Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below.

For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the setup documentation.

  1. Install Claude Code:

    MacOS/Linux (Recommended):

    curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

    Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):

    brew install --cask claude-code

    Windows (Recommended):

    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

    WinGet (Windows):

    winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode

    NPM (Deprecated):

    npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

  2. Navigate to your project directory and run claude.

Plugins

Anthropic's Claude Code plugins are developed in claude-plugins-official. See the plugins directory for more about plugins.

Reporting Bugs

We welcome your feedback. Use the /bug command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a GitHub issue.

Connect on Discord

Join the Claude Developers Discord to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community.

Data collection, usage, and retention

When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the /bug command.

How we use your data

See our data usage policies.

Privacy safeguards

We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training.

For full details, please review our Commercial Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

## What's changed

- Added a record of your answer when Claude Code asks to turn on the mods it writes in a session
- Added `assume_role` on `mantle` upstreams of the Claude apps gateway, for a role in another AWS account and for per-developer AWS cost attribution
- Added an `effort` option to a mod's `$.model.fork`, so a quick side job can run at `low` whatever effort the session uses; the result reports the effort sent
- Added the date a stored claude.ai sign-in ends to `claude auth status` (`loginExpiresAt`) and to `claude -p` JSON results (`credential_expires_at`)
- Added a one-line stderr warning to `claude -p` text output, starting 10 days before a stored claude.ai sign-in ends

releases.name: v2.1.317
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added a warning to `/schedule` when a new cloud scheduled task gets connectors you did not ask for, with how to remove them
- Added a check that asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email address to the network
- Added `onFailure: "block"` for Agent SDK hook callbacks, so a callback that fails blocks the action instead of letting it run
- Added a notice in Claude Desktop's Code tab when your organization's remote managed settings haven't loaded for the session, and another once they do
- Added a notice when auto mode's check has no answer for a subagent's tool call, which used to leave nothing in the main view

- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NESTED_SESSION_

releases.name: v2.1.316
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK`, which turns the `ultrathink` keyword off
- Added pooled group budgets to the Claude apps gateway: one monthly budget that a group's members share, on top of each member's own limit, set with `pooled_budget` on the spend limits admin API
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_LOOPED_CROSS_CERT_DROP` to keep system cross-certificates that certify each other in a loop, for servers whose private CA needs one
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT` to set the effort level subagents run at when nothing else names one, instead of inheriting the session's
- Added `managed.policy_mode: layered` to the Claude apps gateway: every policy that matches a developer applies, each merged over the ones listed below it, not only the first
- Added `guardrail.input_tagging` on Claude apps gateway Bedrock upstreams, which wraps prompts in the input tags that an Amazon Bedrock guardrail's prompt attacks filter needs; `all_messages_and_system` also tags the system prompt
- Deprecated fast mode for Opus 4.8 as of October 30, 2026; it will be removed on November 30, 2026. After removal, fast mode requests on Opus 4.8 return an error and do not fall back to st

releases.name: v2.1.314
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories`: Write, Edit and NotebookEdit refuse paths outside the working directories in every permission mode
- Added an optional `groups` list to Claude apps gateway upstreams: only developers in the listed IdP groups are sent to that upstream, on failover too
- Added `guardrail_trace` to Claude apps gateway Bedrock upstreams, to log which Amazon Bedrock guardrail filter fired on a request, without the matched text
- Added idle compaction to VS Code and Claude Desktop's Code tab: a 200K+ token conversation left idle is summarized, and the summary is used on your next message if the prompt cache has expired
- Fixed sessions failing turn after turn with "Invalid effort level" when an organization's admin caps a model's effort: Claude Code now lowers the effort, retries, and says which level it uses
- Fixed `claude -p` exiting with code 0 and no output when startup failed; it now prints the error and exits 1
- Fixed Bedrock sessions with many images failing every turn and `/compact` with "400 Input is too long." instead of removing older images and compacting
- Fixed Microsoft Foundry sessions failing when the resour

releases.name: v2.1.312
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `oidc.user_id_claim` to the Claude apps gateway, to identify people by an id_token claim other than `sub`, such as Microsoft Entra ID's `oid`
- Added click to send: in fullscreen, clicking the "to send now" hint under a queued message sends it right away, as its key does
- Fixed managed settings and organization policy not being fetched for the rest of the session after signing in from the VS Code extension
- Fixed Claude overwriting a very large CLAUDE.md, rules file or @-included file in a subdirectory after seeing only its start; Write now asks Claude to read it all or edit in place
- Fixed per-directory and `paths:` skills not being found after a Bash `cd` deeper into a git repository
- Fixed a rare case where the first reply after resuming a session in the terminal could be missing the next time the session was resumed

aiSummary.oneLiner: An official, terminal-based AI coding assistant powered directly by the Claude model family.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claude Code is a command-line interface tool developed by Anthropic that deeply integrates their Claude AI models directly into a developer's local environment. It is designed to understand entire codebases by autonomously navigating directories, reading files, and executing local shell commands for context. The tool assists with complex refactoring, bug hunting, and feature implementation without requiring developers to leave their terminal or copy-paste code into a browser. It maintains a secure, local execution perimeter while leveraging the advanced reasoning capabilities of models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet. This drastically reduces context switching and accelerates the software development lifecycle.
keyFeatures: Native terminal integration: Operates entirely within the command line, integrating seamlessly into existing shell environments and workflows.
Autonomous codebase navigation: Capable of searching directories, reading files, and grepping for specific patterns to build context automatically.
Local command execution: Safely runs local tests, linters, and build scripts to verify code changes before finalizing them.
Advanced model reasoning: Powered directly by Anthropic's most capable models, ensuring high-quality architectural advice and code generation.
Context-aware refactoring: Understands the broader repository structure, allowing it to safely execute multi-file changes and updates.

useCases.title: Automated Bug Resolution
useCases.description: Instruct the assistant to locate the source of a specific error trace, write the fix, and run the test suite to verify it.

useCases.title: Complex Code Refactoring
useCases.description: Command the tool to migrate an entire directory of components to a new framework API across multiple interdependent files.

useCases.title: Codebase Onboarding
useCases.description: Ask the terminal assistant to explain the architecture and data flow of a massive, unfamiliar repository dynamically.

useCases.title: Rapid Feature Implementation
useCases.description: Describe a new feature in natural language and allow the tool to scaffold the necessary files, logic, and tests automatically.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Professional software engineers and developers who prefer working in terminal environments and want powerful, context-aware AI assistance. It requires familiarity with command-line interfaces and local development workflows.
